mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 5.0%) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing the cost of capital and increasing equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if the 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS < 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) signals monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and reducing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if the 20-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) rises above 5.0% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) rises above 200.0, it indicates a combination of monetary tightening and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if the 20-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where both FEDFUNDS > 5.0% and CPIAUCSL > 200.0.

mechanism_narrative: In a labor market tightening regime, a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE < 4.5%) signals strong employment conditions, boosting consumer confidence and spending, which leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if the 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE < 4.5% and the regime is labor market tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST > 1400.0) indicates strong consumer demand for residential construction, typically leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if the 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where HOUST > 1400.0.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) rises above 110.0 and GDP growth (GDPC1) is positive, it indicates robust economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if the 20-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where both INDPRO > 110.0 and GDPC1 > 0.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the federal funds rate above 5.0% (FEDFUNDS > 5.0%) within the last 10 days signals imminent monetary tightening, typically leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if the 5-day S&P 500 returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 5.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS > 370000.0) indicates strong consumer spending, typically leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The mechanism fails if the 60-day S&P 500 returns are negative in more than 60% of instances where RSAFS > 370000.0.
